title: Vaccine reactions: expected vs call
summary: Mild reactions after vaccines are common. Know what is typical and what is not.
whatsNormal:
Vaccines teach the immune system to recognize germs. Mild reactions mean the body is responding.

• Soreness, redness, or small lump at the injection site for 1–2 days
• Low-grade fever or fussiness for 24–48 hours after some vaccines
• Sleepier or clingier for a day, still waking for feeds
• Rotavirus vaccine can rarely cause loose stools for a few days

Comfort measures: extra cuddles, fluids as usual, and acetaminophen only if your pediatrician recommended it for your baby's age and weight.
watchFor: Fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher in a baby under 3 months, always call, even after vaccines
High fever lasting more than 48 hours after a vaccine
Non-stop crying for 3+ hours or an unusual high-pitched cry
Hives, swelling of face or lips, or trouble breathing within hours of a vaccine
callDoctorIf: Signs of allergic reaction: rash with hives, wheezing, or swelling, seek emergency care for breathing difficulty
Injection site redness spreading or with red streaks
You are unsure whether symptoms are vaccine-related, your clinic can guide you
disclaimer: Enfold provides general educational information. It does not replace professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. If you think your child has a medical emergency, call your local emergency number immediately.
